items.followUp: Write any three characteristics of a compound.

rubric.why: Checks that a compound has a constant composition.
rubric.description: States that the elements in a compound are combined in a fixed ratio or proportion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a fixed ratio, proportion or definite composition.

rubric.why: Checks that a compound has properties of its own.
rubric.description: States that a compound has properties different from those of its constituent elements.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this difference in properties.

rubric.why: Checks the uniform nature of a compound.
rubric.description: States that a compound is homogeneous or has uniform composition throughout.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for homogeneity or uniform composition.

rubric.why: Distinguishes chemical separation from physical separation.
rubric.description: States that the elements of a compound can be separated only by chemical methods.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for separation by chemical methods.

rubric.why: Checks a characteristic property of a pure compound.
rubric.description: States that a pure compound has definite melting and/or boiling points.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a definite melting point or boiling point.

modelAnswer: A compound has a definite composition: its elements are combined in a fixed ratio.
Its properties are different from the properties of its constituent elements.
It is homogeneous and has uniform composition throughout.
Its elements can be separated only by chemical methods, not by physical methods.
A pure compound has definite melting and boiling points.

items.followUp: Explain the formation of magnesium chloride by transfer of electrons.

rubric.why: Checks the definition of an ionic bond.
rubric.description: Defines an ionic bond as the electrostatic force of attraction between oppositely charged ions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the electrostatic attraction definition.

rubric.why: Checks the outer-shell electron arrangements relevant to the transfer.
rubric.description: Identifies that sodium has one outer-shell electron and chlorine has seven.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct electron arrangements or equivalent outer-shell information.

rubric.why: Checks the direction of electron transfer.
rubric.description: States that sodium transfers its outer electron to chlorine.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing the transfer from sodium to chlorine.

rubric.why: Checks the ions formed and their role in the compound.
rubric.description: States that Na⁺ and Cl⁻ form and their attraction produces ionic NaCl.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correctly charged ions and their attraction forming NaCl.

modelAnswer: An ionic bond is the electrostatic force of attraction between oppositely charged ions.
A sodium atom has the electronic configuration 2,8,1, while a chlorine atom has 2,8,7.
Sodium transfers its one outer-shell electron to chlorine.
Sodium forms Na⁺ and chlorine forms Cl⁻.
The electrostatic attraction between these ions forms ionic NaCl.

items.followUp: State any three postulates of Bohr's atomic model.

rubric.why: Checks Bohr's proposed paths for electrons.
rubric.description: States that electrons revolve around the nucleus in circular orbits.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the circular-orbit postulate.

rubric.why: Checks that only particular orbits are allowed.
rubric.description: States that electrons can occupy only certain permitted orbits or energy levels.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the permitted-orbit postulate.

rubric.why: Checks the energy condition for an electron in a stationary orbit.
rubric.description: States that an electron in a permitted stationary orbit has definite energy and does not radiate energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for definite energy and no radiation in a stationary orbit.

accept: moves from one permitted orbit to another
rubric.why: Checks how an electron changes energy level.
rubric.description: States that an electron absorbs or emits energy when it moves between permitted orbits.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for energy absorption or emission during an orbit change.

rubric.why: Checks the naming or relative energies of Bohr's orbits.
rubric.description: Identifies shells such as K, L and M, or states that electron energy is greater in an orbit farther from the nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correct shell naming or the increase in energy with distance.

modelAnswer: Electrons revolve around the nucleus in circular orbits.
Electrons can occupy only certain permitted orbits, called energy levels or shells.
An electron in a permitted stationary orbit has a definite energy and does not emit or absorb energy.
An electron absorbs or emits energy when it jumps from one permitted orbit to another.
The orbits are designated K, L, M and so on; the energy of an electron is greater in an orbit farther from the nucleus.

items.followUp: Define solubility and state how temperature affects the solubility of solids and gases.

rubric.why: Checks the central meaning of solubility.
rubric.description: Defines solubility as the maximum amount of solute that dissolves.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the maximum-amount definition.

rubric.why: Checks the conditions included in the definition.
rubric.description: Specifies 100 g of solvent, a particular temperature and formation of a saturated solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for these defining conditions.

rubric.why: Checks the usual temperature effect on solid solutes.
rubric.description: States that the solubility of most solids in liquids increases as temperature rises.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the increase in solubility of most solids.

rubric.why: Checks the contrasting temperature effect on gases.
rubric.description: States that gas solubility in liquids generally decreases as temperature rises.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the decrease in gas solubility.

modelAnswer: Solubility is the maximum amount of solute that dissolves in 100 g of a solvent at a particular temperature to form a saturated solution.
The solubility of most solid solutes in liquids increases with an increase in temperature.
The solubility of gases in liquids generally decreases with an increase in temperature.

items.followUp: Define one atomic mass unit in terms of the carbon-12 atom.

rubric.why: Checks the fractional value in the definition.
rubric.description: States that one atomic mass unit is one-twelfth of the reference atom's mass.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the one-twelfth fraction.

rubric.why: Checks that the correct reference atom is named.
rubric.description: Identifies the reference atom as carbon-12.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming carbon-12.

modelAnswer: One atomic mass unit (amu) is defined as one-twelfth of the mass of one carbon-12 atom.
